purpose:
You are a senior developer working on rocm-distro-tester. This is a fresh checkout of the repository. Analyze the project in depth, including the most recent commits, and deliver an overview before any follow-on work begins.
provides an overview of where to look and what each area is responsible for.

instructions.instruction: Read the docs in intent order: README.md (what this is), PLAN.md (how it is designed — note which Section each script implements), INSTALL.md (target deployment), TODO.md (the handoff task sheet), HISTORY.md (why it exists).
Review the last 20 commits (git log --oneline, then read the interesting diffs) to establish what was built or changed most recently and which work stream is active.

Verify the codebase against its own claims before trusting it: - bash -n every shell script in scripts/ and ci-trigger/scripts/ - python3 -m py_compile on each poller in ci-trigger/*.py - python3 -m pytest ci-trigger/tests/ -q (note: the dashboard test module needs Flask installed; failures there are environmental, not regressions)

Classify every component as production-grade, in-progress, or draft. Draft code is characterized by: syntax errors, references to files that do not exist, or behavior contradicting PLAN.md. List each finding with file path and line number. Do not fix anything during this analysis.

Cross-check the three pillars against their PLAN.md sections: registries (Section 6) -> setup_docker_registry.sh, pin_infra_images.sh, docker-compose*.yml; state DB (Section 7) -> setup_db.sh, verify_db_setup.sh, schema plans; pollers (Section 1) -> ci-trigger/poll_*.py. Flag any drift between plan and code.
End the report with a short list of suggested next steps, ordered the way PLAN.md's own phased delivery sequence would suggest them.
If any instruction is confusing, suggest three better at the end of the report.
If any aditional data is needed, request it at the end of the report.

project-context: An automation layer on top of the manual rocm-distro-containers test suite (~1,200 Dockerfiles across 8 distros). Turn "someone manually tests ROCm on the lab GPUs" into a scheduled, parallel, reproducible service with an auditable record.

repo-layout.description: Directory map of the rocm-distro-tester repository. Scripts are the product; .md files are contract; tests mirror scripts.
repo-layout.base-dir-relative-to: The repository root. Runbooks, compose files for the two registry tiers and the interim dashboard, and the prompts/ corpus live here.
repo-layout.structure: <directory name="prompts" type="directory" desc="Self-contained XML prompts for pi, invoked as: pi < prompt-file">
repo-layout.related-repositories: <repository name="rocm-distro-containers" location="~/rocm/rocm-distro-containers" desc="The manual test suite this project automates. Per-distro layout: ////. Its 'copr-preview-pkgdiff' and friends are the pattern for what eventually lands in pkg-tests/. Prompts used to run those tests live in ~/ai/fedora-pi-prompts (test/, mock/, fedora-review/) — they are being migrated into this repository's prompts/test/ as test content is migrated." />
repo-layout.environment:
Development and deployment run on AMD hardware (Strix Halo + Radeon Pro W7900) with SELinux-Enforcing hosts and a small pool of GPU tester nodes. All AI tooling is on-premise (pi-coding-agent with Ollama). Nothing here talks to external LLM services.
Network landmarks (do not renumber): - rocm-builder:5000 — test-tier registry (all testers trust) - rocm-builder:5001 — infra-tier registry (builder/db roles only) - state:8443 — planned state-svc (PLAN §7.3, not yet built) - rocm-builder:5432 / host 5002 — postgres / dashboard - /rocm-builder, /rocm-db — dedicated storage roots per role
